children.text:
Oṃ bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ śṛṇuyāma devāḥ bhadraṃ paśyemākṣabhir yajatrāḥ |
sthirair aṅgais tuṣṭuvāṃsas tanūbhir vyaśema devahitaṃ yadāyuḥ |
svasti na indro vṛddhaśravāḥ svasti naḥ pūṣā viśvavedāḥ |
svasti nas tārkṣyo 'riṣṭanemiḥ svasti no bṛhaspatir dadhātu |
Oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ |
children.translated_text: Oṃ! May we hear what is auspicious with our ears, O gods! May we see what is auspicious with our eyes, O worshipful ones! With firm limbs and bodies, may we, praising [the gods

, enjoy the lifespan allotted by the gods! May <s>Indra</s> of great fame grant us well-being! May <s>Pūṣan</s>, the all-knowing, grant us well-being! May <s>Tārkṣya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>), who removes obstacles, grant us well-being! May <s>Bṛhaspati</s> grant us well-being!]

children.text: oṃ
children.translated_text: Oṃ.

children.text: athāśvalāyano bhagavantaṃ parameṣṭhinam upasametyovāca |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Āśvalāyana</s> approached the Blessed Lord <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) and said:

children.text: adhīhi bhagavan brahmavidyāṃ variṣṭhāṃ sadā sadbhiḥ sevyamānāṃ nigūḍhām |
children.translated_text: "Teach me, O Blessed Lord, the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmavidyā</s>), the highest, that which is always cultivated by the good, and which is hidden —

children.text: yathācirāt [yayācirāt] sarvapāpaṃ vyapohya parātparaṃ puruṣaṃ yāti vidvān ||1||
children.translated_text: by which a wise person, quickly removing all sin, attains the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person) who is beyond the beyond." || 1 ||

children.text: tasmai sa hovāca pitāmahaś ca śraddhā-bhakti-dhyāna-yogād avaihi |
children.translated_text: To him the Grandfather (<s>Brahmā</s>) said: "Know [it] through faith, devotion, meditation, and <s>yoga</s>.

children.text: na karmaṇā na prajayā dhanena tyāgenaike amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ ||2||
children.translated_text: Not by action, nor by progeny, nor by wealth — by renunciation alone have some attained immortality." || 2 ||

children.text: pareṇa nākaṃ nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ vibhrājate yad yatayo viśanti |
children.translated_text: "Beyond heaven, set in the cave [of the heart], it shines — that which the ascetics enter.

children.text: vedānta-vijñānasuniścitārthāḥ saṃnyāsayogād yatayaḥ śuddhasattvāḥ ||3||
children.translated_text: Those ascetics whose understanding is firmly established through the knowledge of <s>Vedānta</s>, purified in nature through the <s>yoga</s> of renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>) —" || 3 ||

children.text: te brahmalokeṣu parāntakāle parāmṛtāḥ [parāmṛtāt] parimucyanti sarve |
children.translated_text: "They, at the time of the great end, are fully liberated beyond immortality in the worlds of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: viviktadeśe ca sukhāsanasthaḥ śuciḥ samagrīvaśiraḥśarīraḥ ||4||
children.translated_text: Seated comfortably in a secluded place, pure, with neck, head, and body held straight —" || 4 ||

children.text: antyāśramasthaḥ sakalendriyāṇi nirudhya bhaktyā svaguruṃ praṇamya |
children.translated_text: "Being in the final stage of life (<s>āśrama</s>), restraining all the senses, bowing with devotion to one's own teacher,

children.text: hṛtpuṇḍarīkaṃ virajaṃ viśuddhaṃ vicintya madhye viṣadam [viśadaṃ] viśokam ||5||
children.translated_text: meditating on the heart-lotus — stainless, pure, clear, sorrowless —" || 5 ||

children.text: acintyam avyaktam anantarūpaṃ śivaṃ praśāntam amṛtaṃ brahmayonim |
children.translated_text: "Unthinkable, unmanifest, of infinite form, auspicious, peaceful, immortal, the source of <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: tam ādimadhyāntavihīnam ekaṃ vibhuṃ cidānandam arūpam adbhutam ||6||
children.translated_text: without beginning, middle, or end, the One, all-pervading, consciousness-bliss, formless, wonderful —" || 6 ||

children.text: umāsahāyaṃ parameśvaraṃ prabhuṃ trilocanaṃ nīlakaṇṭhaṃ praśāntam |
children.translated_text: "Accompanied by <s>Umā</s>, the Supreme Lord, the Master, three-eyed, blue-throated, peaceful —

children.text: dhyātvā munirgacchati bhūtayoniṃ samastasākṣiṃ tamasaḥ parastāt ||7||
children.translated_text: meditating [on Him], the sage attains the source of all beings, the witness of all, beyond darkness." || 7 ||

children.text: sa brahmā sa śivaḥ sendraḥ so 'kṣaraḥ paramaḥ svarāṭ |
children.translated_text: He is <s>Brahmā</s>, He is <s>Śiva</s>, He is <s>Indra</s>, He is the imperishable, the supreme, the self-sovereign.

children.text: sa eva viṣṇuḥ sa prāṇaḥ sa kālo 'gniḥ sa candramāḥ ||8||
children.translated_text: He alone is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, He is <s>Prāṇa</s> (the life-breath), He is Time, He is Fire, He is the Moon. || 8 ||

children.text: sa eva sarvaṃ yad bhūtaṃ yac ca bhavyaṃ sanātanam |
children.translated_text: He alone is everything — what has been and what will be, the eternal.

children.text: jñātvā taṃ mṛtyum atyeti nānyaḥ panthā vimuktaye ||9||
children.translated_text: Knowing Him, one crosses beyond death. There is no other path to liberation. || 9 ||

children.text: sarvabhūtastham ātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani |
children.translated_text: Seeing the Self dwelling in all beings, and all beings in the Self,

children.text: saṃpaśyan brahma paramaṃ yāti nānyena hetunā ||10||
children.translated_text: beholding the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, one attains [liberation] — not by any other means. || 10 ||

children.text: ātmānam araṇiṃ kṛtvā praṇavaṃ cottarāraṇim |
children.translated_text: Making the Self the lower fire-stick and <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ) the upper fire-stick,

children.text: jñānanirmathanābhyāsāt pāpaṃ [pāśaṃ] dahati paṇḍitaḥ ||11||
children.translated_text: through the repeated churning of knowledge, the wise one burns away sin [or: bondage]. || 11 ||

children.text: sa eva māyāparimohitātmā śarīram āsthāya karoti sarvam |
children.translated_text: He alone, the Self deluded by <s>Māyā</s>, taking on a body, performs all [actions].

children.text: striyannapānādivicitrabhogaiḥ sa eva jāgrat paritṛptim eti ||12||
children.translated_text: Through the varied enjoyments of women, food, drink, and the rest, He alone in the waking state attains satisfaction. || 12 ||

children.text: svapna [svapne] sa jīvaḥ sukhaduḥkhabhoktā svamāyayā kalpitajīvaloke |
children.translated_text: In dream, that <s>jīva</s> (individual self) is the experiencer of happiness and sorrow, in a world of beings created by his own <s>Māyā</s>.

children.text: suṣuptikāle sakale vilīne tamo 'bhibhūtaḥ sukharūpam eti ||13||
children.translated_text: In deep sleep, when all has dissolved, overcome by darkness, he attains the form of bliss. || 13 ||

children.text: punaśca janmāntarakarmayogāt sa eva jīvaḥ svapiti prabuddhaḥ |
children.translated_text: And again, through the force of <s>karma</s> from previous births, that very <s>jīva</s> sleeps and awakens.

children.text: puratraye krīḍati yaśca jīvas tatas tu jātaṃ sakalaṃ vicitram ||14||
children.translated_text: The <s>jīva</s> who plays in the three cities [of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep] — from Him all this varied [creation] has arisen. || 14 ||

children.text: dhāramānandam akhaṇḍabodhaṃ yasmiṃl layaṃ yāti puratrayaṃ ca ||14*||
children.translated_text: The support, the bliss, the undivided consciousness — in whom the three cities dissolve. || 14* ||

children.text: etasmāj jāyate prāṇo manaḥ sarvendriyāṇi ca |
children.translated_text: From Him arises <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath), mind, and all the senses,

children.text: khaṃ vāyur jyotir āpaḥ pṛthivī viśvasya dhāriṇī ||15||
children.translated_text: space, wind, fire, water, and earth — the supporter of the universe. || 15 ||

children.text: yat paraṃ brahma sarvātmā viśvasyāyatanaṃ mahat |
children.translated_text: That which is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the Self of all, the great abode of the universe,

children.text: sūkṣmāt sūkṣmataraṃ nityaṃ tat tvam eva tvam eva tat ||16||
children.translated_text: subtler than the subtle, eternal — That you are, you are That. || 16 ||

children.text: jāgratsvapnasuṣuptyādiprapañcaṃ yat prakāśate |
children.translated_text: That which illuminates the phenomenal world of waking, dreaming, deep sleep, and the rest —

children.text: tad brahmāham iti jñātvā sarvabandhaiḥ pramucyate ||17||
children.translated_text: knowing 'I am that <s>Brahman</s>,' one is freed from all bondage. || 17 ||

children.text: triṣu dhāmasu yad bhogyaṃ bhoktā bhogaś ca yad bhavet |
children.translated_text: In the three states, whatever is enjoyed, the enjoyer, and the enjoyment —

children.text: tebhyo vilakṣaṇaḥ sākṣī cinmātro 'haṃ sadā śivaḥ ||18||
children.translated_text: different from all these, the witness, pure consciousness alone — I am ever <s>Śiva</s> (the Auspicious). || 18 ||

children.text: mayy eva sakalaṃ jātaṃ mayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam |
children.translated_text: In me alone is everything born, in me all is established,

children.text: mayi sarvaṃl layaṃ yāti tad brahmādvayam asmy aham ||19||
children.translated_text: in me all dissolves — I am that non-dual <s>Brahman</s>. || 19 ||

children.text: iti
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first section.

children.text: prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ ||
aṇor aṇiyān aham eva tadvan mahān ahaṃ viśvam ahaṃ vicitram |
children.translated_text: "I am smaller than the smallest and likewise I am the greatest. I am the universe, I am the wondrous.

children.text: purātano 'haṃ puruṣo 'ham īśo hiraṇmayo 'haṃ śivarūpam asmi ||20||
children.translated_text: I am the ancient, I am the <s>Puruṣa</s>, I am the Lord, I am golden, I am of the form of <s>Śiva</s>." || 20 ||

children.text: apāṇipādo 'ham acintyaśaktiḥ paśyāmy acakṣuḥ sa śṛṇomy akarṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: "Without hands or feet am I, of inconceivable power. I see without eyes, I hear without ears.

children.text: ahaṃ vijānāmi viviktarūpo na cāsti vettā mama cit sadāham ||21||
children.translated_text: I know, being of distinct form; yet there is no knower of me — I am ever consciousness." || 21 ||

children.text: vedair anekair aham eva vedyo vedāntakṛd vedavid eva cāham |
children.translated_text: By many <s>Vedas</s> I alone am to be known; I am the maker of the <s>Vedānta</s> and the knower of the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text: na puṇyapāpe mama nāsti nāśo na janma dehendriyabuddhir asti ||22||
children.translated_text: Neither merit nor sin is mine; there is no destruction for me, no birth, no body, no senses, no intellect. ||22||

children.text: na bhūmir āpo na ca vahnir asti na cānilo me 'sti na cāmbaraṃ ca |
children.translated_text: There is no earth, no water, no fire for me; there is no wind, nor is there space for me.

children.text: evaṃ viditvā paramātmarūpaṃ guhāśayaṃ niṣkalam advitīyam ||23||
children.translated_text: Having known thus the nature of the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), dwelling in the cave [of the heart], without parts, without a second, ||23||

children.text: samastasākṣiṃ sadasadvihīnaṃ prayāti śuddhaṃ paramātmarūpam ||23*||
children.translated_text: the witness of all, beyond existence and non-existence — one attains the pure nature of the Supreme Self. ||23*||

children.text: yaḥ śatarūdrīyam adhīte so 'gnipūto bhavati sa vāyupūto bhavati, sa ātmapūto bhavati sa surāpānāt pūto bhavati sa brahmahatyātpūto bhavati sa suvarṇasteyāt pūto bhavati sa kṛtyākṛtyāt pūto bhavati tasmād avimuktam āśrito bhavaty āśramī sarvadā sakṛd vā japet |
children.translated_text: Whoever recites the <s>Śatarudrīya</s> becomes purified by fire; he becomes purified by wind; he becomes purified in the Self; he becomes purified from the drinking of liquor; he becomes purified from the killing of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; he becomes purified from the theft of gold; he becomes purified from deeds done and undone. Therefore, he becomes one who has taken refuge in the <s>Avimukta</s> [Kāśī], an <s>āśramin</s> (one established in a stage of life). He should recite it always, or even once.

children.text: anena jñānam āpnoti saṃsārārṇavanāśanam |
children.translated_text: By this one obtains knowledge that destroys the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence).

children.text: tasmād evaṃ viditvainaṃ kaivalyaṃ padam [phalam] aśnute |
children.translated_text: Therefore, having known this thus, one attains <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute liberation) — the supreme state [fruit],

children.text: kaivalyaṃ padam [phalam] aśnute ||24||
children.translated_text: one attains <s>kaivalya</s>, the supreme state [fruit]. ||24||

children.text: ity atharvavede kaivalyopaniṣat samāptā ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Kaivalyopaniṣad</s> of the <s>Atharvaveda</s>.

children.text: oṃ tat sat
children.translated_text: Oṃ tat sat.
